# ANALYSIS: STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND_REGIME_STRATIFICATION

**Filed:** 2026-08-20  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** regime_stratification_analysis  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)  

## Hypothesis

The STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND veto's benefit (removing wrong-way trades) may be regime-dependent. We hypothesize that the veto is most effective in high-VIX, strong-trend regimes (where wrong-way trades are more prevalent) and less effective or neutral in low-VIX, ranging regimes (where trend classification is noisy and wrong-way trades are rarer). The goal is to quantify whether the veto's OOS P&L and Sharpe improvements are consistent across VIX/trend buckets or concentrated in specific regimes.

## Mechanism

Split the full OOS period (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) into 9 buckets by:  
- VIX regime: low (<15), medium (15-25), high (>25)  
- Trend regime: uptrend, downtrend, range (as defined by `crypto.lib.market_structure.classify_trend` on 5m same-day data)  

For each bucket, compute:  
- Base engine OOS P&L and Sharpe  
- Veto-enabled engine OOS P&L and Sharpe  
- Delta P&L and delta Sharpe (veto minus base)  
- Edge_capture contribution (if any J anchor days fall in the bucket)  

Since the OP-16 edge_capture is defined only on the 6 J anchor days, we will also map each J anchor day to its VIX/trend bucket to see if the veto fired on those days and what the P&L impact was.
